standard.title: Observing and Measuring
standard.description: make and record observations, including informal measurements, using digital tools as appropriate
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can make observations using their senses (F band). They now extend to making observations more systematically and recording them using informal measurements and digital tools.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students make and record observations using text, drawing, counts, informal measurements (cups, handspans, paces, blocks) and digital tools (photography, video) as appropriate.

nodes.label: Observations are made and recorded systematically
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make observations using their senses and appropriate tools, record observations using at least two formats (drawing, count, informal measurement, digital photo), and explain what an observation is.
nodes.minimum_width: Students make and record observations in two different formats for a given investigation.
nodes.typical_width: Students explore what an observation is through guided discussion; make observations using senses and tools; use informal measurements (cups, handspans, paces, blocks, string) to record quantities; photograph or video observations; and organise recorded observations in tables or drawings.
wider: Use informal measurements such as blocks to measure plant growth or paces to measure how far an object has moved — applying informal measurement to quantify observations
Record observations through text, drawing, counts, informal measurements and digital photography — building a repertoire of recording formats
Explore how digital photography can capture observations that are hard to record by hand — comparing recording tools
success_criteria: Makes and records observations in at least two different formats (e.g. drawing and informal measurement)
Explains what an observation is in their own words
